title: The Arrow and the Song
sub: Learn it a piece at a time. Every level gives you a little less, and the picture for the line you are on stays with you the whole way — so by the last level the picture alone is enough.

lines.t: I shot an arrow into the air,
It fell to earth, I knew not where;
For, so swiftly it flew, the sight
Could not follow it in its flight.
I breathed a song into the air,
It fell to earth, I knew not where;
For who has sight so keen and strong,
That it can follow the flight of song?
Long, long afterward, in an oak
I found the arrow, still unbroke;
And the song, from beginning to end,
I found again in the heart of a friend.

levels.name: Last words
levels.tag: One blank at the end of each line
levels.blurb: The whole poem is in front of you and only the last word of each line is missing. The picture for the line you are on sits underneath from the start, so the two begin to go together.

levels.name: First words
levels.tag: One blank at the start of each line
levels.blurb: Now the first word of each line is gone. Starting a line is the bit people get stuck on when they stand up to recite — and the picture is still there beside you.

levels.name: Half gone
levels.blurb: About half the words are away now, spread through the poem. The shape of it is still there to lean on, and so is the picture.

levels.name: Line by line
levels.blurb: One whole line at a time, with the rest of the poem still around it. Look at the picture first and see whether the line comes.

levels.name: By heart
levels.blurb: No words on the screen at all — just the pictures you have had beside you the whole way up, one for each line, and you say it from memory.
